A and B are located on the same horizontal grid line, C is located to the lower right of B, and the circular arc passes from near A through B and then to near C. The problem gives the coordinates A(0,4), B(2,4), C(4,2). Reasoning: The center of the circle M must lie on the perpendicular bisector of any chord. First look at chord AB: A(0,4), B(2,4), whose midpoint is ((0+2)/2,(4+4)/2)=(1,4). AB is a horizontal line, so the perpendicular bisector of AB is the vertical line x=1. Then look at chord BC: B(2,4), C(4,2), whose midpoint is ((2+4)/2,(4+2)/2)=(3,3). The slope of BC is (2-4)/(4-2)=-1, so the slope of its perpendicular bisector is 1, and the equation is y-3=1(x-3), namely y=x. Combining x=1 and y=x, obtain y=1. Therefore the coordinates of the center of the circle M are (1,1).

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: it shows a Cartesian grid with a circular arc passing through the labeled points A, B, and C; A and B lie on the same horizontal grid line, and C is down-right from B. From the text, use A(0,4), B(2,4), and C(4,2). Since the center of a circle lies on the perpendicular bisector of every chord, take chord AB: its midpoint is (1,4), and because AB is horizontal, its perpendicular bisector is x=1. Then take chord BC: its midpoint is (3,3), slope of BC is (2-4)/(4-2)=-1, so the perpendicular bisector has slope 1 and equation y-3=x-3, i.e. y=x. Intersect x=1 with y=x to get M=(1,1).
